stem: A spherical gold nanoparticle has a radius of $2.50\text{~nm}$. Assuming gold crystallizes in a face-centered cubic structure with a density of $19.3\text{~g/cm}^{3}$, how many gold atoms ($M = 197.0\text{~g/mol}$) are present in a single nanoparticle?
The speed of light is $3.00 \times 10^{8}\text{~m/s}$. Express this speed in furlongs per fortnight. ($1\text{~furlong} = 201.168\text{~m}$; $1\text{~fortnight} = 14\text{~days}$).
Which of the following statements represents an intensive physical property?
choices: The total heat capacity of a sample of water is $418.4\text{~J/K}$.
A sample of copper has a volume of $12.5\text{~mL}$.
The standard boiling point of ethanol is ${78.37}^{\circ}\text{C}$.
The mass of a gold bar is $1.00\text{~kg}$.

stem:
Perform the following calculation and express the answer to the correct number of significant figures:

$$\frac{(14.285 - 0.0821) \times 0.05200}{3.14159 + 0.002}$$

A hydrometer measures liquid density. A cylindrical piece of cork ($d = 0.240\text{~g/cm}^{3}$) with length $10.0\text{~cm}$ and cross-sectional area $1.50\text{~cm}^{2}$ floats vertically in a fluid of density $1.20\text{~g/cm}^{3}$. How much length of the cork is submerged below the liquid surface?

A container weighs $22.10\text{~g}$ when empty, $45.50\text{~g}$ when filled with water ($d = 0.998\text{~g/mL}$ at $20^{\circ}\text{C}$), and $51.20\text{~g}$ when filled with an unknown liquid at the same temperature. What is the density of the unknown liquid?
Which of the following processes represents a chemical change?
choices: Dissolution of sodium chloride in water
Tarnishing of silver cutlery in air

stem: The temperature on a newly devised temperature scale, $_{}^{\circ}X$, is related to the Celsius scale by $_{}^{\circ}X = 1.50( \circ C) + 20.0$. What is the absolute zero temperature ($- {273.15}^{\circ}\text{C}$) on the $_{}^{\circ}X$ scale?
Homogeneous mixtures are distinguished from pure substances because homogeneous mixtures:
choices: Can be separated into simpler substances using physical methods.
Have a fixed composition regardless of preparation.
Consist of only one type of atom.
Cannot exist in the gaseous phase.

stem: A sheet of platinum foil has dimensions $2.50\text{~cm} \times 4.00\text{~cm}$ and a mass of $1.076\text{~g}$. Given the density of platinum is $21.45\text{~g/cm}^{3}$, what is the thickness of the foil in micrometers ($\mu\text{m}$)?

In J.J. Thomson’s cathode-ray tube experiment, the mass-to-charge ratio ($m/e$) of the electron was determined. If Robert Millikan determined the charge of an electron to be $- 1.602 \times 10^{- 19}\text{~C}$ and $e/m = - 1.76 \times 10^{8}\text{~C/g}$, what is the mass of a single electron?

An atom of the radioactive nuclide $_{92}^{238}\text{U}$ undergoes decay by emitting an alpha particle ($\alpha$), followed by two consecutive beta particles ($\beta^{-}$). What is the resulting daughter nuclide?

Naturally occurring chlorine consists of two stable isotopes: $_{}^{35}\text{Cl}$ ($34.9688\text{~amu}$) and $_{}^{37}\text{Cl}$ ($36.9659\text{~amu}$). The average atomic mass of chlorine is $35.4527\text{~amu}$. What is the percent abundance of $_{}^{37}\text{Cl}$?
How many protons, neutrons, and electrons are present in a single ${_{}^{59}\text{Ni}}^{3 +}$ ion?
Rutherford’s gold foil experiment demonstrated that:
choices: Electrons orbit the nucleus in fixed energy levels.
Electrons are embedded in a uniform sphere of positive charge.
Most of the mass and all positive charge of an atom are concentrated in a tiny dense nucleus.
Neutrons exist in equal numbers to protons in stable nuclei.

stem: Which pair represents isotopes of the same element?
An element $\text{X}$ forms a compound with oxygen having the formula $\text{X}_{2}\text{O}_{3}$, which contains $30.06\%$ oxygen by mass. Identify the element $\text{X}$.
Which of the following species is isoelectronic with the argon atom ($\text{Ar}$)?

An unknown element $\text{M}$ has three naturally occurring isotopes: $\text{M} - 24$ ($23.9850\text{~amu}$, $78.99\%$), $\text{M} - 25$ ($24.9858\text{~amu}$, $10.00\%$), and $\text{M} - 26$ ($25.9826\text{~amu}$, $11.01\%$). Calculate the atomic weight of $\text{M}$ and identify the element.
How many total electrons are in a nitrate ion ($\text{NO}_{3}^{-}$)?
